conflicts.fact: Runner B's velocity during the slow middle section of the marathon and Runner A's velocity (and the resulting relative speed)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2: Runner A ~19 km/h, Runner B ~17.6 km/h in the 25–35 km section, and ~22 km/h in the final sprint. Lesson 5: Runner B drops from ~5.6 m/s (20 km/h) to 4.9 m/s (17.6 km/h), then 6.2 m/s (~22.3 km/h) in the sprint. Lesson 7 Observe/Explain: Runner A 19 km/h, Runner B 17.6 km/h, relative speed 1.4 km/h. Lesson 7 Model Building: Runner A 21 km/h, Runner B 17 km/h, relative speed 4 km/h, said to be taken from the Lesson 6 v-t graph.

conflicts.fact: Where and when Runner A overtook Runner B, and whether Runner B was ahead at 30 km
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3: Runner A overtakes Runner B during the slow section between 30 km and 35 km (the lines cross after 30 km). Lesson 4: Runner B leads (steeper gradient) and the water-station segment is horizontal, i.e. gradient 0. Lesson 7 Model Building: the overtake happens with about 4 km to go, around km 38. Lesson 7 Explain: Runner A closes a 200 m gap at 1.4 km/h, which takes ~8.6 min, yet the overtake is placed in the 25–35 km section.

conflicts.fact: Whether a horizontal gradient on a displacement-time graph (water station) is consistent with the description of the race
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says runners slow at water stations; Lesson 4 annotates a horizontal (gradient 0, stationary) water-station segment; Lesson 6 describes 'water station slow-downs'. Lesson 1 Observe places the water station near 30 km, while the Lesson 2 slowdown is 25–35 km. Elite runners stopping completely is inconsistent with the dataset.

conflicts.fact: Runner B's early velocity vs. uniform motion label and the 'sprint' segments
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 Model Building labels Runner B's first 10 km as uniform motion even though Lesson 2 says velocity surges above 21 km/h there, and labels 40–42 km as non-uniform while the overview gives a sprint over the final 2 km only. Lesson 5 says the steep positive gradient is between km 35 and 42, and Lesson 5's table shows a sprint in the final 2 km.

conflicts.fact: Class race course and data collection distances/intervals
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 Overview says measured distances of 40 m and 80 m, but the Observed section and Model Building say a 40 m course with times at 10 m intervals. Lesson 6 describes a 400 m race at Nakuru High School with a 60 s duration, inconsistent with a 400 m race time for school athletes (60 s at 2 s intervals, with a sprint in the last 10 s).

conflicts.fact: Marathon route and the time at which the table was recorded
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: start and finish both on Uhuru Highway, the route runs from the Kenya National Theatre along Uhuru Highway and loops back, with runners along Kenyatta Avenue. Lesson 5 places a matatu at Kencom on Moi Avenue/Uhuru Highway. Lesson 8's split table includes marks at 0, 5, ..., 40 and 42 km, and Lesson 8 asks for 'time in minutes'.

conflicts.fact: Cumulative model contents built in earlier lessons
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says the model currently contains a displacement-time sketch from Lesson 3. Lesson 6 says that in Lessons 4–5 they added displacement-time graphs and speed calculations, while Lesson 3 is where displacement-time graphs were added and Lesson 5 added velocity-time sketches.

conflicts.fact: Gradient of velocity-time graph and 'distance-time' graphs and area meaning
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 refers to velocity-time graphs as a third tool 'alongside distance-time and displacement-time graphs', but the sequence only taught displacement-time graphs. Lesson 6 says area = distance (displacement), a conflation of the terms distinguished in Lesson 1.
